_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Mathematics unit lecture film, Lesson 5 Telling the Time. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson page's own teaching order - units of time swapped both ways, reading the face, writing a 12-hour time in 24-hour, the bus timetable, the interval counted on in hops, and days over the end of a month - and every number is the lesson's own: 4 hours is 240 minutes, the face reads 4:40, 15:45 is 3:45 in the afternoon, Hodan's Bus B reaches School at 08:55, 10:40 to 12:15 is 1 hour 35 minutes, and 28 April plus 9 days is 7 May.
title: Telling the Time
subtitle: Grade 4 Mathematics
objectives: Understand the direct relationship between units of time, and convert between them.
Read and record time accurately in digital notation (12- and 24-hour) and on analogue clocks.
Interpret and use the information in timetables (12- and 24-hour clock).
Find time intervals between different units: days, weeks, months and years seconds, minutes and hours that do not bridge through 60.

beats.say: A clock has two hands, and each one tells you something different.
Read them properly and you can catch a bus, or time a programme.
Time does not count in tens. It counts in sixties.
Sixty seconds make one minute, and sixty minutes make one hour.
Twenty-four hours make one whole day, from midnight to midnight.
Four hours is four lots of sixty minutes, which is 240 minutes.
To go back the other way, you divide. 240 divided by 60 is 4 hours.
Here is a clock. The short hand and the long hand do different jobs.
The short hand gives the hour. It is sitting between 4 and 5.
Take the hour it has passed. So the hour is 4, not 5.
The long hand gives the minutes. Every number on the face is five minutes.
It points at the 8, and eight fives are 40. The time is 4:40.
A timetable never says a.m. or p.m. It uses 24-hour time instead.
Morning hours stay as they are. Quarter past nine is written 09:15.
After midday, add 12 to the hour. Half past three becomes 15:30.
So 15:45 is 3:45 in the afternoon. Take the 12 off again.
Midday is written 12:00. Midnight is written with four zeros.
This is a real bus timetable, and every time on it is 24-hour.
Read down a column to follow one bus all the way to school.
Read across a row to see when every bus reaches that one stop.
Hodan must be at school by nine o'clock. Which is the latest bus?
Bus C does not arrive until 10:40, far too late. Bus B gets there at 08:55.
How long did something last? Count on from the start to the end.
The programme starts at 10:40 and ends at 12:15.
Count on 20 minutes to 11:00, then one whole hour to 12:00.
Then 15 minutes more. That is 1 hour and 35 minutes altogether.
Never take the times away like ordinary numbers. An hour is 60 minutes.

scenes.heading: Over the end of the month

beats.say: Days work the same way. It is 28 April, and you add 9 days.
April has 30 days. There is no 37 April.
Two days take you to the 30th, the last day of April.
Seven days are left over, so they go into May. It is 7 May.
Time counts in sixties: 60 seconds, 60 minutes, and 24 hours in a day.
The short hand gives the hour, and each number is five minutes.
After midday add 12, and a timetable reads down and across.
To find how long, count on in hops, and days carry into the next month.
